LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "No Inter line runs longer than 65 characters" uses "line" for a typeset row. The brief and the checks themselves use "line" for a piece of copy ("the members line", "all three lines of the end card copy"). On the animation this makes H022 look like it contradicts H002: the members line is about 96 characters, and its first sentence alone is about 71, so it can only pass if it wraps. An annotator who reads "line" as the copy line will fail every correct end card.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: channel-animation/H022: "No single row of Inter text on the end card of “Animated channel title and end card” (channel-animation.mp4) is longer than 65 characters; longer copy wraps onto more rows." On the other eight checks, write "No single row of Inter text on “Name” (file) is longer than 65 characters."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: These checks guard the planned long-title/short-title trap in staticfox_titles.txt. The retired exact pixel sizes came back as "about one seventh" or "about one thirteenth of the frame height". That is still a measurement, and "about" gives no tolerance, so nobody can tell 1/7 from 1/6 by eye. The checks also use spec jargon a designer will not know ("the full display size", "the reduced long-copy size"). On the long titles the check also packs two ideas into one: a named size mode and a fraction. The fractions themselves are correct: in the supplied Anton-Regular.ttf, cap height is 1760/2048 em, so 190 px type gives capitals about 163 px tall (about 1/6.6 of the frame) and 96 px type gives about 82 px (about 1/13).
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Short titles (01 to 04): "On “Name” (file.png), each Anton setup capital measures roughly 145 to 180 px tall on the 1080 px frame." Long titles (05, 06): "On “Name” (file.png), each Anton setup capital measures roughly 70 to 95 px tall on the 1080 px frame." Remove the phrases "full display size" and "reduced long-copy size". Optionally add one visible check on 05 and 06 for the rule "the whole stack drops": "All Anton rows of the title on “Name” (file.png) are the same size."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Compound check: the font family (Archivo Black Regular) and "at its normal width, not condensed" are independent facts. Archivo Black squeezed narrower by horizontal scaling passes the family test and fails the width test. The type-system rule "Never set the payoff word condensed" is its own rule, separate from the scale role.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Keep the family in the existing id: "The final word “MAP” on “Channel thumbnail - WE BROKE THE MAP” (thumbnail-we-broke-the-map.png) is set in Archivo Black Regular." Add one new check per output: "The final word “MAP” on “…” (thumbnail-we-broke-the-map.png) is not squeezed narrower than the supplied Archivo Black letters." Use the same pattern on the other eight checks, and keep the "If a title stack appears" condition on the two teasers.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "Displayed 320 px wide, the title ... is fully visible, with no letters cut off at an edge" ties a clipping check to a display size. Scaling the image down cannot crop letters, so the 320 px condition means nothing here and suggests a resize step that is not needed. It also makes the check read like a near-duplicate of the new 320 px readability check (H033/H032/H031) on the same file. The coverage table already uses these ids for F14 (no clipped characters), not for the 320 px test.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: "No letter of the title on “Channel thumbnail - WE BROKE THE MAP” (thumbnail-we-broke-the-map.png) is cut off at the frame edge." Do the same on the other five thumbnails. Leave the 320 px wording only on the readability check.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: channel-animation/H019 ("STATIC" at the 190 px display size, not the 96 px long-copy size) is retired with covered_by H009 (STATIC FOX is the largest text) and H017 (STATIC is Anton Regular). The task's required_content for channel-teaser-vertical says: "Shots from at least three of the six supplied captures, all of them also used in the wide teaser". The brief also says "from the same cut". So "all of them also used" is the stated requirement. Loosening it would weaken the check.

rejected.why: Rejected the "holds still" part; the split was accepted. Reviewer A showed that no brief or commission text asks the teasers for a still hold. The group requirement says only "The final frame is a usable end card." I kept both teasers on "closes on an end card frame" so they match.

rejected.finding: A (teaser setup size): Option 1 says to state the upright teaser size as a fraction of the frame width.

unresolved: The validator gives 9 warnings about pixel values on the cap-height range checks (thumbnail H017/H018, channel-animation/H019, channel-teaser/H021, channel-teaser-vertical/H019). This is deliberate. These checks guard the planned long-title/short-title trap, so they cannot be dropped. The ranges need an on-screen ruler, not eyeballing. The 145 to 180 px and 70 to 95 px ranges do not overlap, so a measurement settles each one. A human lead should confirm that annotators are allowed to measure with a ruler.

I did not add the enlargement (pixelation) check to the two teasers. They have no expert_review_criteria (the field is None), and the planned trap is about a thumbnail punch-in. A softened shot from capture 03 or 05 in a teaser is therefore not checked. Coverage F16 marks both teaser cells na with that reason.
